newsitem.title: USA: CME Oct hogs down two cent limit, commercials sell.
newsitem.headline: CME Oct hogs down two cent limit, commercials sell.

text.p: CME October hogs fell their daily two-cent-a-lb limit as commercial selling helped to trigger sell-stops, floor sources said.

Talk that this week's advance in cash hogs may be much more modest than many had expected helped to weigh on the market. At 1228 CDT October hogs were locked the two cent limit down, offered at 73.925 cents a lb.
There had been widespread talk late last week that cash hogs would rise by around $3 per cwt this week with packers margins moving into the black as pork prices strengthened.

Dealers noted, however, after modest gains on Monday and Tuesday there were already some signs the run-up in cash hogs was running out of steam amid talk that recent light kills may have left a backlog of slaughter-ready hogs.
Other months were down 1.950 to 0.750 cent.
Pork bellies were also sharply lower to the three cent limit down, with February offered limit down at 75.550 cents, depressed by a weaker cash fresh pork belly market.
